title: Exact localization of fixed tensor and its normalized resolving comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], homotopy category $K(R)$ and unbounded derived localization $Q_h:K(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the triangulated structure of $K(R)$ and the exact functor $Q_h$ of [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Use the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the resolving full subcategory $\mathcal P_R$ of flat-term K-flat complexes, and the published bifunctor $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ with its specified natural comparison $c_{P,S}:Q_h\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R S)\cong T(Q_hP,Q_hS)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Fix a K-flat complex $A$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Assume the fixed tensor operations $H_A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R B)$ and $H^A(B)=\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_R A)$ induce additive exact functors on $K(R)$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], invert quasi-isomorphisms after applying $Q_h$, and use the coherent signed shift maps $s^2_n,s^1_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts].
There exist additive exact functors $G_A,G^A:D(R)\to D(R)$ and natural isomorphisms $\eta_L:Q_hH_A\cong G_AQ_h$ and $\eta_R:Q_hH^A\cong G^AQ_h$. Their coherent integer-shift comparisons are the unique ones for which $\eta_L,\eta_R$ commute with shifts and restrict to $Q_hs^2_n,Q_hs^1_n$, with the canonical shift comparisons of $Q_h$ inserted. The functors carry every distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle with its connecting arrow.
There are unique natural isomorphisms $d_L:G_A\cong T(Q_hA,-)$ and $d_R:G^A\cong T(-,Q_hA)$ for which $(d_L)_{Q_hP}(\eta_L)_P=c_{A,P}$ and $(d_R)_{Q_hP}(\eta_R)_P=c_{P,A}$ for every $P\in\mathcal P_R$. If $r:P\to B$ is any quasi-isomorphism with $P\in\mathcal P_R$, the composite comparisons $e_L=(d_LQ_h)\eta_L$ and $e_R=(d_RQ_h)\eta_R$ have components
$$e_{L,B}=T(1,Q_hr)c_{A,P}(Q_hH_A(r))^{-1},\qquad e_{R,B}=T(Q_hr,1)c_{P,A}(Q_hH^A(r))^{-1}.$$
These formulas are independent of $r$ and are natural for every derived varying-argument map through $d_L,d_R$. The factorization with its signed shifts and normalized comparisons is unique up to its unique compatible natural isomorphism. No boundedness or flatness of cohomology is required.

proof.text: Let P be the published resolving class and L=P.ι⋙Q. Its published localization-equivalence witness supplies an equivalence F₀ with V.Q⋙F₀≅L, where V is the quasi-isomorphisms restricted to P. Composition with an equivalence and transport along this isomorphism make L a localization. This is resolving_isLocalization.

source.place: Categories Tags 04VG/04VK; sites-cohomology Tag 06YU, resolving presentation

proof.text: Treat either fixed tensor H simultaneously. Localize H⋙Q to G₀ and η₀:H⋙Q≅Q⋙G₀. The natural resolving comparison c yields b:L⋙G₀≅L⋙F by composing η₀ inverse with c. Extend b along L to d₀:G₀≅F. Put η=η₀ followed by Qd₀; the liftNatTrans component formula proves η_P=c_P. Use the published F itself as the final descended functor G, and take d to be its identity isomorphism.

source.place: Categories Tags 04VG/04VK, transformation descent; sites-cohomology Tag 06YU

proof.text: Use Functor.commShiftOfLocalization for the lifting η inverse to give F coherent integer shifts. The localization theorem also proves η inverse, and hence η, commutes with shifts. Expanding the composite shift comparisons is exactly ShiftCompatible. For another shift structure with that square, cancel η at shifted objects and F applied to the canonical Q shift map. Localization.natTrans_ext along Q gives equality of all shift isomorphisms, hence equality of the structures.

source.place: Categories Tag 04VK; Mathlib CategoryTheory/Shift/Localization.lean, commShiftOfLocalization and NatTrans.commShift_iso_hom_of_localization

proof.text: The functors H and Q are triangulated. Q.mapArrow is essentially surjective, as for the derived localization. Apply Functor.isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso to η inverse: F is triangulated for the shift structure just constructed, including the connecting morphism. The proved Mathlib instance Functor.IsTriangulated gives F.Additive. Thus no separate additive-descent lemma is required.

source.place: sites-cohomology Tag 06YU, exact derived tensor; Mathlib CategoryTheory/Triangulated/Functor.lean, isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso and IsTriangulated additive instance

proof.text: The identity isomorphism d:F≅F is normalized because η_P=c_P. Any other normalized d′ has η_P d′_(QP)=η_P; cancel η_P and apply Localization.natTrans_ext along L to obtain d′=id.

For any quasi-isomorphism f:P→B, naturality of η gives (H⋙Q)(f) η_B=η_P F(Qf). Its first factor is invertible by hU; multiply by that inverse and substitute η_P=c_P. This gives exactly the stated invertedMapIso formula. Each expression equals η_B, so the formula is independent of any chosen resolution. The Lean conclusion quantifies over every such resolution and requires no separate construction of one.

source.place: sites-cohomology Tag 06YU, comparison on resolutions; naturality and inversion

proof.text: Given another factorization η′:H⋙Q≅Q⋙G′, lift the identity of H⋙Q using the two lifting comparisons to θ:F≅G′. The component formula gives η_X θ_(QX)=η′_X. After precomposition with Q its shift compatibility is that of η inverse followed by η′; cancel the canonical Q shift maps and use natTrans_ext to obtain compatibility globally. Restrict θ followed by d′ to L; normalization and cancellation of η_P give the identity there, hence everywhere. Any θ′ with the required comparison agrees on Q by cancellation of η_X, and natTrans_ext proves uniqueness.

source.place: Categories Tag 04VK, full faithfulness and compatible uniqueness

proof.text: Apply normalizedDescent to the left and right fixed tensor functors. In each case construct c by evaluating resolvingComparison at (A,P) or (P,A), where A is resolvingObject A hA hAf. Its naturality is the published two-variable naturality evaluated on (id,f) or (f,id). The given CommShift structures retain the signed normalization recorded by hSL and hSR; no change to those hypotheses is needed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06YU and Categories Tags 04VG/04VK. Lean proof by M1: use the published tensor itself as the final descent, extend its comparison by localization, descend coherent shifts with Mathlib commShiftOfLocalization, and obtain additivity from isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso. Normalization, resolution formula, and compatible uniqueness are proved by component calculations and localization faithfulness.

Step 3, I type-checked a_n: G((QB)[n]) -> GQ(B[n]) -> QH(B[n]) -> (QHB)[n] -> (GQB)[n], extended by clause (2) with identity comparisons. Step 4, the zero and addition laws hold by conjugation and clause (3). Step 5, I re-derived the connecting square from the Step 3 normalization and the naturality of eta at w, then TR1. Steps 6-7, L = J composed with the fraction localization is a localization; b_P = c_{A,P} eta_P^-1 is natural on P_R and extends uniquely. Step 8, naturality of e at a resolution r gives the formulas, QH(r) is invertible by hypothesis, and independence of r is equality to e_B. Edge cases: n=0, the sign (-1)^{np} on the left side only, zero complexes, r=id gives c, unbounded complexes.
